media.transcript: This is a day in the life being stranded on an island in Thailand. I began the day by going online and making about £12. I had to move rooms because mine was fully booked. And this bad boy sent me back about £8. And honestly, for the price, you really can't complain. The downside is that means we've only got £4 left to our name. And of course, the room comes equipped with the most important item you're going to need out here. So as of right now, my visa's run out, which is a big problem. Every day that I don't extend it, I'm going to have to pay £12. But the only way to extend my passport is to get it back from the bike shop. Problem is, I've lost the key to the bike nearly a week ago. And a new key plus what I owe on the bike comes to a whopping £7,100 bar. Which is £162 that we don't have. Once I pay that off, I can get my passport back and extend my visa. After talking to the bike shop owners, I can't get a new key until I pay everything off. So me and Juni decided to get a smoothie. And this place has over 100 combinations. After grabbing my smoothie, I went to grab a seat and actually met a really cool puppy. And I'm not going to lie, I think he was a bit excited to see me. I reckon we need to come up with a name for this little dude. I'm thinking of something like Scrappy or Rodrigo. So obviously, time's really ticking. Day one of being over my visa, which means one thing. We really have to make some bread. And lo and behold, we actually got two donos here. Both are very kind and encouraging words. So I want to say a huge shout out to you guys. With a new sense of hope in my heart, me and my friend Yan decide to whip it up to a local restaurant to get some cheap grub. An average meal here only costs like £1.50. And the portion size is really good. They got some cool decorations inside as well. Some very nice photographs hanging on the wall. So in this place, you actually have to write your order down yourself. Obviously, I went ahead and ordered myself the cheapest thing on the menu. I went ahead and grabbed myself a pork fried rice, along with a can of Fanta that only sent me back £1.80 altogether. Yan went for the exact same thing. But his drink order made me feel like he's got an extra set of door keys on him. But you know what? Fair play. I know there's a lot of confusion about whether or not I'm going back to the UK, staying in Asia or going to Australia. But right now, that's up in the air. We got to focus on one thing at a time if we're going to make any serious progress. Right now, we just need to hit a £200 budget, clear the debt we have with the bike shop, get our passport back, and then pay to extend my visa. But like I say, each day we don't do that, we're going to be charged an extra £12. I don't know. There was a problem with Yan's bike, so we decided to go back to the hostel where he picked up a shiny golden new one. And bro, I don't think I've ever seen a cooler moped in my life. Yan then invited me up to go to the beach. I needed to do some editing anyway. So we made a nice half an hour drive to a beach called Zen Beach. This place is pretty cool. It's got drum circles going on. And honestly, a pretty good view for the sunset. Today's the first time in a while that I've actually felt like I've made some decent progress. I'm feeling super motivated to be back, even if it is in the context of being caught in a little bit of a disaster. All I know is we've made it this far, so why not keep going? Like they say, Rome wasn't built in a day. But if you guys do want to support the journey, check out my bio.

media.transcript: ¿Alguna vez te has preguntado cómo es la comida china de China? ¿Existe realmente el arroz tres delicias? Pues hoy te lo voy a enseñar. Acompáñame a uno de los restaurantes más típicos y tradicionales de Shanghai. Y es que mirad qué vistas más impresionantes tiene hacia el Bund. Pero como ya veis, no solo las vistas impresionan, sino que la presentación de todos sus platos están sumamente cuidados. Las bebidas están deliciosas, pero a lo que vamos, a la comida. Empezamos con el Hong Sauro, que básicamente esto es panceta y uno de mis platos favoritos. Aquí en Shanghai sí que se nota que lo hacen un pelín más dulce porque es su estilo. Seguimos con unas verduras chinas salteadas y un pollo cocido servido en frío. Creerme que esto está súper rico y la salsa le da todo el sabor. Sencillo, pero muy rico. Y esto seguro ya que casi todo el mundo lo conoce. Son los Shaolong Paos rellenos de cerdo y cangrejo, que son un básico. Y casi tan famoso como los Shaolong Paos, el pez ardilla. Y no, no te preocupes, es una aluguna frita con salsa gris dulce. Pedimos una panceta salteada picante, que esto no es típico de Shanghai, pero está muy rico. Seguimos con las gambas borrachas, súper gracioso porque están marinadas con vino. Y una sopita de patata. Y ya llegamos a la parte que más me gusta, el postre. Tenían demasiada variedad, pero bueno, empezamos por los mochis. Yo diría que son unos mochis que estaban bastante ricos. También pedimos otro postre de tofu, que me sorprendió porque no me lo esperaba para nada. Y luego este pudin de matcha, que estaba riquísimo. Pero es que tan solo la presentación ya me había ganado. Un poco de frutita y más mochi. Acabamos súper llenos y todo esto nos costó como unos 15 euros por persona. Así que guárdatelo para tu próximo viaje a Shanghai.
